subject: Creating a list of all possible rounded values of a vector

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Creating a list of all possible rounded values of a vector
parts:
I have a vector of numeric values, and I want to make a list of vectors, which contains all combinations rounding each value in the list up or down.

It’s a bit hard to explain; the method below does it. (Actually, it returns a data frame, but I can still use lapply() across the columns, which is my next step). However, it’s rather clunky and this could be a bottleneck in my code. Anyone have an idea how to do it in a faster/more elegant way?

the_vector = c(3.3, 7.8, 10.2)
the_list = as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(macro_state), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))))
​

Here is a different approach. (But this is not less complicated. LOL)

require(dplyr)

rounded_list <- 
  as.data.frame(the_vector) %>%
  mutate(floor = floor(the_vector), ceiling = ceiling(the_vector)) %>%
  select(floor, ceiling) %>%
  do(as.data.frame(t(.))) %>%
  do(as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(.))))

Bonnie

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Creating a list of all possible rounded values of a vector
parts: My 2c:

the_vector = c(3.3, 7.8, 10.2)
the_list = as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))))

library(microbenchmark)
# you can speed things up by passing some args to expand.grid
noams <- microbenchmark(
  the_list <- as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))))
)

noams_use_eg_better <- microbenchmark(
  the_list <- as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))),
                                          stringsAsFactors=FALSE, KEEP.OUT.ATTRS=FALSE
                                          ))))
rbind(noams,noams_use_eg_better)
#    min      lq     mean   median      uq      max neval cld
# 559.203 605.864 714.6965 631.8340 738.262 1592.066   100   b
# 297.220 320.450 395.2017 334.8495 497.588  707.499   100  a

## but much more savings if you hack expand.grid to just return the list you want
## (since it constructs list internally before casting to data.frame
## for good measure, I excised all the stringsAsFactors and KEEP.OUT.ATTRS portions

eg <- function (... )
{
    nargs <- length(args <- list(...))
    if (!nargs)
        return(as.data.frame(list()))
    if (nargs == 1L && is.list(a1 <- args[[1L]]))
        nargs <- length(args <- a1)
    if (nargs == 0L)
        return(as.data.frame(list()))
    cargs <- vector("list", nargs)
    iArgs <- seq_len(nargs)
    nmc <- paste0("Var", iArgs)
    nm <- names(args)
    if (is.null(nm))
        nm <- nmc
    else if (any(ng0 <- nzchar(nm)))
        nmc[ng0] <- nm[ng0]
    names(cargs) <- nmc
    rep.fac <- 1L
    d <- sapply(args, length)
    orep <- prod(d)
    if (orep == 0L) {
        for (i in iArgs) cargs[[i]] <- args[[i]][FALSE]
    }
    else {
        for (i in iArgs) {
            x <- args[[i]]
            nx <- length(x)
            orep <- orep/nx
            x <- x[rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac,
                nx)), orep)]
            cargs[[i]] <- x
            rep.fac <- rep.fac * nx
        }
    }
    do.call(Map, c(c, cargs))
}

hacked_eg <- microbenchmark(
  my_list <-   eg(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))
)
rbind(noams,noams_use_eg_better, hacked_eg)
#     min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval cld
# 559.203 605.8640 714.6965 631.8340 738.2620 1592.066   100   c
# 297.220 320.4500 395.2017 334.8495 497.5880  707.499   100  b
# 150.168 155.7235 164.3659 159.2490 165.9545  374.378   100 a 

library(testthat)
expect_equal(unname(the_list), unname(as.data.frame(my_list)))
# output matches up to names

Actually, you the same savings by using the `do.call(Map, c(c, expand.grid(...)))` construct
without the hacking of expand grid itself! See below

(In combination with expand.grid args of course,
it's those that make the real difference)

- Jaime

noams_mapped <- microbenchmark(
 mapped_list <- do.call(Map, c(c, expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))),
                                          stringsAsFactors=FALSE, KEEP.OUT.ATTRS=FALSE
                                          ))))

library(testthat)
expect_equal(unname(the_list), unname(as.data.frame(mapped_list)))


rbind(noams,noams_use_eg_better, noams_mapped, hacked_eg)

#     min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval cld
# 559.203 605.8640 714.6965 631.8340 738.2620 1592.066   100   c

On Fri, Jul 10, 2015 at 11:22 AM, Jaime Ashander <jash...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
My 2c:

the_vector = c(3.3, 7.8, 10.2)
the_list = as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))))

library(microbenchmark)
# you can speed things up by passing some args to expand.grid
noams <- microbenchmark(
  the_list <- as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))))
)

noams_use_eg_better <- microbenchmark(
  the_list <- as.data.frame(t(expand.grid(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))),
                                          stringsAsFactors=FALSE, KEEP.OUT.ATTRS=FALSE
                                          ))))
rbind(noams,noams_use_eg_better)
#    min      lq     mean   median      uq      max neval cld
# 559.203 605.864 714.6965 631.8340 738.262 1592.066   100   b
# 297.220 320.450 395.2017 334.8495 497.588  707.499   100  a

## but much more savings if you hack expand.grid to just return the list you want
## (since it constructs list internally before casting to data.frame
## for good measure, I excised all the stringsAsFactors and KEEP.OUT.ATTRS portions

eg <- function (... )
{
    nargs <- length(args <- list(...))
    if (!nargs)
        return(as.data.frame(list()))
    if (nargs == 1L && is.list(a1 <- args[[1L]]))
        nargs <- length(args <- a1)
    if (nargs == 0L)
        return(as.data.frame(list()))
    cargs <- vector("list", nargs)
    iArgs <- seq_len(nargs)
    nmc <- paste0("Var", iArgs)
    nm <- names(args)
    if (is.null(nm))
        nm <- nmc
    else if (any(ng0 <- nzchar(nm)))
        nmc[ng0] <- nm[ng0]
    names(cargs) <- nmc
    rep.fac <- 1L
    d <- sapply(args, length)
    orep <- prod(d)
    if (orep == 0L) {
        for (i in iArgs) cargs[[i]] <- args[[i]][FALSE]
    }
    else {
        for (i in iArgs) {
            x <- args[[i]]
            nx <- length(x)
            orep <- orep/nx
            x <- x[rep.int(rep.int(seq_len(nx), rep.int(rep.fac,
                nx)), orep)]
            cargs[[i]] <- x
            rep.fac <- rep.fac * nx
        }
    }
    do.call(Map, c(c, cargs))
}

hacked_eg <- microbenchmark(
  my_list <-   eg(lapply(as.list(the_vector), function(z) c(floor(z), ceiling(z))))
)
rbind(noams,noams_use_eg_better, hacked_eg)
#     min       lq     mean   median       uq      max neval cld
# 559.203 605.8640 714.6965 631.8340 738.2620 1592.066   100   c
# 297.220 320.4500 395.2017 334.8495 497.5880  707.499   100  b
# 150.168 155.7235 164.3659 159.2490 165.9545  374.378   100 a 

library(testthat)
expect_equal(unname(the_list), unname(as.data.frame(my_list)))
# output matches up to names
